summary: Chunking can hang indefinitely when maxBatch is not a positive finite integer.

findings.title: Invalid maxBatch causes a non-terminating drain loop
findings.body: The loop assumes config.maxBatch is a positive finite number. If it is 0, negative, NaN, or otherwise invalid, i may never advance toward ids.length, causing drain() to loop indefinitely and consume memory or CPU.
findings.recommendation: Validate config.maxBatch before the loop as a positive finite integer and fail fast with a clear configuration error.

samples.summary: The worker can hang indefinitely when maxBatch is zero or negative.

findings.title: Unvalidated chunk size can cause an infinite loop
findings.body: The loop increments i by config.maxBatch without verifying that it is a positive integer. A zero value prevents i from advancing, while a negative value moves it away from the termination condition, causing drain() to loop indefinitely and consume memory whenever ids is nonempty.
findings.recommendation: Validate config.maxBatch before the loop and throw a configuration error unless it is a positive integer.

samples.summary: Chunking trusts an unvalidated configuration value that can hang the worker or silently lose the batch.

findings.title: Invalid maxBatch can hang or discard work
findings.body: The loop uses config.maxBatch as both its increment and slice width without verifying that it is a positive integer. A value of 0 or a negative value makes the loop non-terminating for any non-empty batch; a missing, non-numeric, or fractional value can produce empty or inconsistent chunks and silently omit IDs.
findings.recommendation: Validate maxBatch before the loop with Number.isInteger(config.maxBatch) && config.maxBatch > 0, and throw a clear configuration error when invalid.
